# ADR-1122: A pull request must kill every mutant in the functions it changes

## Status

accepted; item 6 added by owner decision 2026-11-06 (the verdict is scoped to changed lines). Amends ADR-1115 ("No mutation run is part of the pipeline", owner rule 2026-10-22: mutation testing is scoped to the files a PR changes, never a whole tree). Uses ADR-0770 (`mutation_check.sh`) and ADR-0771 (registered equivalents).

## Context

Owner directive 2026-11-04: a created PR must pass the tests, the e2e tests and the mutation testing without a failure.

Measured on main on 2026-11-05: `scripts/mutation_check.sh` on one 365-line module (`mcp_server/core/ast_extractors.py`, four test files) takes 64 s and exits 1, because the module carries survivors older than any open PR (for example `_extract_python_func`, `_walk_for_calls`). A gate on the changed file would therefore fail every PR that touches it, for code the PR did not write.

Prior art: Google mutates only the lines a change touches and reports the result in review (Petrovic and Ivankovic, "State of Mutation Testing at Google", ICSE-SEIP 2018, doi 10.1145/3183519.3183521; Petrovic et al., "Practical Mutation Testing at Scale", arXiv 2102.11378).

## Decision

1. `scripts/ci_unit.sh` ends with `scripts/ci_mutation_diff.py`, so the `unit` job (and its coverage run) carries the mutation gate. `ci.json` keeps its five keys. Outside a pull request (`GITHUB_BASE_REF` empty) the step does nothing.
2. The script fetches the base branch, reads `git diff -U0 FETCH_HEAD...HEAD` (the merge base, so a base branch that moves on adds nothing) for `mcp_server/**/*.py`, and keeps the top-level functions and methods whose lines the PR changed, decorators and trailing blank lines included. An added line that is blank or only a comment changes nothing and selects no function, unless it sits inside a multiline string or its hunk replaced code; otherwise the blank lines above a new function, which fall in the span of the function before it, selected that function (#878: `count_reranked`). A deletion of a whole top-level definition selects nothing; a deletion inside a function selects it. mutmut cannot mutate lines, so the granularity is the function, the finest unit it names. The deletion of a whole method selects nothing in its class, the deletion of a nested function selects its enclosing function. A changed function whose decorators mutmut 3.8.1 cannot mutate (anything but `staticmethod` and `classmethod`) produces no mutant at all, so it is reported as a `::warning::` and not gated.
3. Per changed file, the tests are the unit test files that import the module (`tests_py/scripts`, `integration`, `benchmarks` excluded). Imports are read with `ast`, so a parenthesized multiline import counts. A changed function whose module no test imports fails the job.
4. `mutation_check.sh` runs once per file with `MUTATION_ONLY_PREFIXES` and passes one `<prefix>*` name per changed function to `mutmut run`, so only the mutants of the changed functions run (`scripts/ci_mutation_scope.py`). mutmut 3.8.1 asserts when no mutant matches those names; after a failed run the gate passes only if mutmut's stats file exists (the stats run succeeded) and the `.meta` file of every mutated file exists and holds no mutant in scope; any other failure fails the job, and so does a failure of the helper that builds the names (it never falls back to running every mutant). `mutation_equivalents.py` drops survivors and registry entries outside those prefixes. What remains is judged as before: every survivor is a registered equivalent (`memory/mutation-equivalents.json`, pinned to its diff) or the job fails. A mutant in scope that no test killed (`no tests`, `timeout`, `suspicious`, `not checked`, `segfault`) fails the job too, and mutmut runs with `--max-children 1` because the tests share one database that every test empties. `mutation_check.sh` sets mutmut's `process_isolation` per platform from `scripts/ci_mutation_scope.py`: `forkserver` on Linux, where a mutant forked from the process that ran the suite hangs in torch and is reported as a timeout; `fork` on macOS, where `forkserver` runs the stats in a forked child that aborts in torch MPS. Any other platform stops the gate, since no isolation was measured there. The mutation sandbox copies `benchmarks` because unit tests import it. No wildcard in the equivalents registry, no per-file suppression.
5. Survivors in functions the PR did not change are not this PR's failure; a PR that rewrites such a function owns its mutants.
6. Within a changed function, only the mutants that alter a line the PR changed are judged (owner decision 2026-11-06). mutmut runs every mutant of the function, since it names mutants by function; `scripts/ci_mutation_lines.py` then places each mutant on the source by diffing it against mutmut's unmutated copy of the function (both indexed in `mutants/<path>.spans`), and keeps it when it alters a changed line, or the anchor of a deletion and the line after it. The survivors it leaves out are counted on the log, not judged; registry entries outside those lines are not reported stale; a mutant that cannot be placed stops the gate. A one-line change no longer owns the mutants that were in the function before it: #865 was asked for 102 survivors of `_construct_store`, #878 for 273 across the recall path.

## Consequences

- Metric: surviving unregistered mutants in changed functions at merge: 0 (not measured today).
- Measured end to end on a real diff: touching `_callee_basename` passes in 44 s (its 5 survivors are registered equivalents); touching `_walk_for_calls` fails with 4 unregistered survivors.
- The `unit` job grows with the mutants of the changed functions, not with the size of their files. Before the names were passed, mutmut ran every mutant of the file and the gate judged the changed functions afterwards: #865 (`backend_resolution.py`, 262 mutants) was cancelled at the six-hour job limit after 141 of them, and #877 ran past two hours. Measured on #877's diff (2026-11-06, local macOS arm64, PostgreSQL 18.6 from `launcher_pg_assets`): 36 mutants run instead of 1,164 (`remember.py` 26 of 741, `domain_mapping.py` about 10 of 423), and the gate reaches its verdict in 21 min 15 s, including the stats and clean-test runs. At the measured 0.07 mutants/s of `remember.py`, its 741 mutants would take about 2 h 56 min (extrapolated, not run). No mutant hit mutmut's timeout on macOS (`⏰ 0`), so no wall-clock cap is added; no cap is applied, so no change goes unchecked.
- On the Linux runner, mutmut's default `fork` isolation made the timeouts the verdict: #877's 26 `_resolve_domain` mutants were all `⏰`, and #878 was cancelled at the six-hour limit with 141 `⏰` among 272 `recall.py` mutants and 29 of 29 in `telemetry.py`. Reproduced on 2026-11-06 in an Ubuntu 26.04 aarch64 container set up as `ci.json` "unit" (Python 3.12, PostgreSQL 18.6.1), on the 11 `publish_record__mutmut_1*` mutants of #878: with `fork`, 5 of the first 7 timed out, the child idle in `loss.backward()` (`titans_memory.py`, `py-spy dump`); with `forkserver`, 0 of 11 timed out and the run took 71 s. The same 11 on macOS with `fork`: 0 timed out; one verdict differs between the platforms (`mutmut_17`, killed on Linux, survived on macOS). On macOS, `forkserver` aborts before any mutant runs: the stats run, now in a forked child, imports `sentence_transformers`, whose `torch.backends.mps.is_available()` ends in SIGABRT (`Child exited with code -6`); with `fork` there, the gate run on the same 11 mutants takes 76 s with 0 timeouts.
- Item 6, checked 2026-11-06: the line placement agrees with `mutmut show` on all 245 mutants of `core/telemetry.py` and all 35 of `core/wiki_identity.py` (methods included). End to end on a one-line change to `publish_record` (local macOS, PostgreSQL 18.6): 38 mutants ran, 18 killed, 20 survived on lines the change did not touch; the gate passes and reports the 20 as not judged, where item 4 alone failed it.
- Module-level code (constants, imports) is not mutated by mutmut and is not gated.
